ocr.notes: gist readable but many garbled words in the articles of agreement

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reprinted the Cincinnati Commercial's account of Allen and Joe Goss signing articles at Cincinnati's Empire Saloon to fight for $2,500 a side on September 7, 1876, within 100 miles of the city.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, May 14, 1876; reprinted from the Cincinnati Commercial

facts.fact: Allen and Joe Goss signed articles at the Empire Saloon in Cincinnati to fight under the new London Prize Ring rules for $2,500 a side ($5,000 total)
The Allen-Goss fight was set for Thursday, September 7, 1876, at a place within 100 miles of Cincinnati to be chosen by Ephraim Holland
Ben De Bar backed Allen and put up his stake money; Jack Brown represented Jem Mace, one of Goss's backers
Allen remarked while signing the articles after Goss
facts.quote: Well, I never did like to sign articles first, but here goes.

facts.fact: Allen and Goss went before 'Squire Anthony and bound themselves not to break the peace in Ohio for one year

notes: The summary's '$5,000' is the total purse; each side staked $2,500.
